description: Map domain concept collaborators bidirectionally. When concept A has a collaborator B (non-primitive), concept B should have a corresponding responsibility that references A, describing the same relationship from B's perspective. Primitives (String, Number, Boolean, Date, Integer) are exceptions—they do not require bidirectional mapping.

do.description: Describe the same relationship from both collaborators' perspectives

guidance.description: When A references B as collaborator, B should reference A—mapped perspectives of the same relationship
example: (Campaign generates Voucher → Voucher is generated for Campaign. Same relationship, both perspectives.)

guidance.description: Use responsibility names that describe the relationship from each concept's viewpoint
example: (Each side describes the relationship from its own perspective.)

dont.description: Don't leave collaborator relationships one-way or use mismatched collaborators

guidance.description: Don't have one-way collaborator—if A references B, B should reference A (unless B is primitive)
example: (WRONG: no responsibility referencing Campaign—relationship is one-way)
(Voucher should have a responsibility like 'Generated for a campaign: Campaign')

guidance.description: Don't use mismatched collaborators—the bidirectional pair must describe the SAME relationship
example: (WRONG: 'Inherits metadata' describes a different aspect of the relationship than 'Generates vouchers'. They are not the same bidirectional pair.)
(This maps to Campaign's 'Generates vouchers'—same relationship, both perspectives.)

guidance.description: Don't require bidirectional mapping for primitive collaborators
example: (String is primitive—no need for 'String' to reference Voucher. Primitives are exceptions.)
